keyNote: Findings are keyed on `match_fingerprint`, NOT on `finding_id`. Two scans of the same tree on the same day produced different `finding_id` values for identical findings — the id is regenerated per run, so a baseline keyed on it would fail on every scan and be ignored within a week. The fingerprint is the content address and was byte-identical across both runs.

coverage.note: **This scan was not complete, and a gate that reported otherwise would be the RF-9 shape.** `analysis_completeness.status` is `partial` and `is_complete` is `false`. **The 2026-10-04 run over the design-craft skill set made it worse, not better: 136 of 142 components fully inspected (95.8%), down from 126 of 129 (97.7%).** Six files are `partially_inspected` across four different limits — `static_parse_limit` on `better-accessibility/SKILL.md`, `build-primitive/SKILL.md` and `gate-tiering/SKILL.md`; a `runtime_limit` on `better-typography`; and `obfuscated_instruction_text` on `build-/SKILL.md`, where twelve of the fourteen static analyzers could not finish. `obfuscated_instruction_text` on a document this large is the one worth naming: the deterministic layer declined to evaluate 47 kB of prose containing fenced examples of hostile strings, which is exactly what that file is for. It is recorded as incomplete rather than waved through, because a gate that printed a clean summary over a degraded analyzer would be asserting a coverage it does not have — and the count went **down** when the corpus grew, which is the observation `DESIGN-5` carries.

whyNotClean: A clean baseline with zero entries would be the honest reading of the evidence only if the scanner had run completely and found nothing. It ran completely enough to be informative, and what it found is seven pattern matches against markdown prose — so the correct disposition is a stated reason per finding, which is what this file is. Deleting it and writing 'clean' is the outcome this repository records as RF-9: a number nobody produced.
